title: Relative length of DVR lattices equals determinant valuation
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $K$ be its fraction field, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Let $M\subseteq V$ be an $R$-submodule which is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and whose $K$-linear span is $V$. Let $g:V\to V$ be a $K$-linear isomorphism and put $H=M\cap g(M)$. Write $\ell_R$ for module length [def-weil-pbc-module-length], $\det_K(g)$ for the endomorphism determinant [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant], and $v_R:K^\times\to\mathbf Z$ for the normalized valuation, defined by $v_R(ut^r)=r$ for a unit $u\in R^\times$, a uniformizer $t$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$. Then both $M/H$ and $g(M)/H$ have finite $R$-length, and, regarding those lengths as integers, $$\ell_R(M/H)-\ell_R(g(M)/H)=v_R(\det_K(g)).$$

proof.text: Give M and g(M) their Mathlib Submodule.IsLattice structures. The image is a lattice by finite generation and span_image_linearEquiv. Submodule.IsLattice.inf gives that H = M ∩ g(M) is also a lattice. Over the DVR these lattices are finite free by Submodule.IsLattice.free, and rank' identifies all their R-ranks with the K-rank of V. Thus LinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq supplies an R-linear equivalence e₁:M→H; transport it along the equivalence t:M→g(M) induced by g to obtain e₂=e₁∘t⁻¹:g(M)→H. These choices use proved finite-free-module equivalence theorems, not unproved existence data.

proof.text: For a finite free E and a submodule N equipped with e:E≃N, prove length(E/N)=ord_R(det(N.subtype∘e)). Mathlib's smithNormalFormTopBasis, smithNormalFormBotBasis and smithNormalFormCoeffs diagonalize the inclusion. quotientEquivPiSpan identifies the quotient with the finite product of R/(a_i). Each cyclic length is ord_R(a_i) by the definition of Ring.ord, and length_pi_of_fintype adds these lengths. The diagonal inclusion matrix has determinant ∏a_i, whose order is ∑ord(a_i) by ord_mul'. associated_det_comp_equiv shows that using the original e changes the determinant only by a unit, so ord_eq_of_associated gives the formula. The empty-basis case is included in the finite product and sum formulas.

source.place: DVR case of Tag 02MI, Smith normal form calculation; Tag 00IV for finite products and Tag 02MD for cyclic orders.

proof.text: For lattices N⊆E and e:E≃N, extend an R-basis b of E and b.map e to K-bases using Basis.extendOfIsLattice. Their basis equivalence f:V≃V agrees with e on E, by basis extensionality. Transport e through comapSubtypeEquivOfLe to the submodule N viewed inside E and form its inclusion endomorphism a. Expanding a vector in b proves that the extended K-coordinates are the images under R→K of its R-coordinates; hence toMatrix(f) is the entrywise image of toMatrix(a). RingHom.map_det gives det_K(f)=image(det_R(a)). Its nonvanishing follows because f is invertible. The preceding calculation and Ring.ord_ne_top now give finite length(E/N). Ring.ordFrac_eq_ord and ordMonoidWithZeroHom_eq_ordMonoidHom identify its integer length with log(ordFrac(det_K(f))).

source.place: Tag 02MI, determinant after extending scalars, and Tag 02MD, fraction-field order.

proof.text: Apply the preceding inclusion calculation to H⊆M with e₁ and H⊆g(M) with e₂, obtaining ambient equivalences f₁,f₂ and finite quotient lengths. On every vector of M, f₁(x)=e₁(x)=e₂(g(x))=f₂(g(x)); the extended K-basis of M implies f₁=f₂∘g. Multiplicativity of LinearMap.det gives det(f₁)=det(f₂)det(g). All factors are nonzero, so ordFrac multiplicativity and WithZero.log_mul turn this into log ordFrac det(f₁)=log ordFrac det(f₂)+log ordFrac det(g). Subtract the two integer length formulas. Finally H.comap M.subtype = g(M).comap M.subtype and H.comap g(M).subtype = M.comap g(M).subtype by the membership definitions, giving exactly the two quotients in the statement.
